title: [C10d][NCCL2] Fix NCCL2 CUDA graph cleanup
body:
Destroying NCCL PG with CUDA Graph captured could call ungraphable CUDA APIs (like `cudaGetDevice`) that causes `CUDA error: operation not permitted` (see example code below).
Click here to see the minimal repro script. ```Python """Reproduce nccl2 CUDA graph cleanup failures. Run on a CUDA host with at least two GPUs: torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 repro_nccl2_graph_cleanup.py The default captures 512 collectives, creating more CUDA events than nccl2's default 1,000-event cache can retain when the graph is destroyed. For a single-collective check, run with TORCH_NCCL_CUDA_EVENT_CACHE=0 and --collectives 1. Compare with the legacy backend: torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 repro_nccl2_graph_cleanup.py --backend nccl-legacy """ import argparse import gc import os from datetime import timedelta import torch import torch.distributed as dist def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--backend", choices=("nccl2", "nccl-legacy"), default="nccl2") parser.add_argument("--collectives", type=int, default=512) parser.add_argument("--cycles", type=int, default=2) args = parser.parse_args() if args.collectives < 1 or args.cycles < 1: parser.error("--collectives and --cycles must be positive") rank = int(os.environ["RANK"]) local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]) world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"]) torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank) dist.init_process_group(args.backend, timeout=timedelta(minutes=5)) print( f"rank={rank} backend={args.backend} device={local_rank} " f"cycles={args.cycles} collectives={args.collectives} " f"event_cache={os.getenv('TORCH_NCCL_CUDA_EVENT_CACHE', 'default')}", flush=True, ) try: warmup = torch.ones(1, device="cuda") dist.all_reduce(warmup) torch.cuda.synchronize() for cycle in range(args.cycles): values = torch.full((args.collectives, 1), rank + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() print(f"rank={rank} cycle={cycle} capture", flush=True) with torch.cuda.graph(graph): for value in values: dist.all_reduce(value) values.fill_(rank + 1) graph.replay() torch.cuda.synchronize() expected = world_size * (world_size + 1) / 2 first = values[0].item() last = values[-1].item() if first != expected or last != expected: raise RuntimeError(f"rank={rank} cycle={cycle}: expected {expected}, got {first} and {last}") print(f"rank={rank} cycle={cycle} reset", flush=True) graph.reset() del graph gc.collect() dist.barrier() print(f"rank={rank} cycle={cycle} done", flush=True) finally: dist.destroy_process_group() if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
This PR fixes the `CUDA error: operation not permitted` failure for the cases like above by avoiding ungraphable functions calls. The avoidance was achieved via moving the graph capture work references into a retirement list and then draining the list later when it safe do so, as apposed to the original approach of erasing the work references immediately.
